jobs.occupation: Electronics Engineer
jobs.description:
**Join Trackman’s R&D team and help create world-leading sports tracking solutions

**We are looking for an experienced Electronics Engineer to join our Hardware R&D team and contribute to the development of the next generation of radar- and vision-based products.

At Trackman, we continuously push the boundaries of sports technology. Our products combine radar, computer vision, embedded electronics, and software to deliver market-leading performance analysis solutions used by athletes and organizations worldwide. As part of our Hardware R&D team, you will play a key role in designing and validating advanced electronic solutions that power our innovative products.

**The role

**As an Electronics Engineer, you will work closely with talented colleagues across electronics, mechanics, optics, software, tracking, and production. You will contribute to the development of robust and high-performance hardware solutions from concept through verification and production. This is a hands-on engineering role where technical expertise, curiosity, and collaboration are essential.

**What Will You Be Doing

**

• Develop and verify high- and low-speed digital circuits, including Computer Modules, FPGAs, camera sensors (CMOS), high-performance ADCs and DACs, microcontrollers (MCUs), USB and LAN controllers, and power management ICs.

• Design and develop DC power supply and power management circuits, ensuring efficient and reliable power distribution across hardware platforms.

• Work with DC/DC converter topologies such as Buck, Boost, Buck-Boost, SEPIC, Flyback, and Forward converters.

• Perform laboratory testing, signal analysis, verification, and debugging using oscilloscopes, signal generators, and other advanced measurement equipment.

• Participate in schematic design, PCB layout reviews, stack-up definition, and constraint-driven multilayer PCB development.

• Use simulation tools such as LTspice to validate and optimize designs before hardware implementation.

• Collaborate with mechanical, optical, software, and manufacturing teams to ensure designs meet product requirements and are optimized for production.

• Support production and quality teams in troubleshooting hardware-related issues and implementing improvements to increase product robustness and manufacturing yield.

• Contribute to technical discussions, design reviews, and continuous improvement initiatives across the hardware organization.

**Job Requirements

****What are we looking for?

**

• Bachelor or Master in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related technical field.

• 5+ years of experience developing electronic products and working with design-for-manufacture principles.

• Strong understanding of digital and analog electronics, PCB design, and electronic components.

• Experience with simulation tools such as LTspice or equivalent.

• Hands-on experience with laboratory equipment, including oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, and signal generators.

• Experience developing power management and DC/DC converter solutions is considered an advantage.

• Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with a structured approach to problem solving.

• Ability to work effectively in cross-functional teams and communicate technical topics clearly.

• Familiarity with regulatory and compliance requirements affecting electronic product development.

**The Office

**We are located in our state-of-the-art HQ at DTU Science Park in Hørsholm. We take great pride in the building we designed! The office features bright meeting rooms, coffee areas to catch up with colleagues, a large testing arena with simulators available for employees and a fitness centre, everything surrounded by a beautiful forest and respecting the environment. We made sure to utilize the newest technologies to be energy efficient and mindful of ventilation and sound propagation. The cherry on top is our canteen: with an indoor and outdoor area to enjoy the fresh food prepared by our own kitchen staff.

**Join the home of a powerful sports brand and a one-of-a-kind technology

**Our proprietary technology is based on expert knowledge about radar, computer vision, data, and software engineering. Our solutions are developed by specialists who endlessly explore and challenge new technical boundaries. Trackman’s blend of cutting-edge technology, sports, and continued growth make our company an outstanding place to work.

Our work culture is entrepreneurial, ambitious, and rewarding as you get to collaborate with inspiring colleagues and interact with the leaders of golf, baseball, and football. Based on a unique brand reputation, we are proud to work in close partnership with the top athletes, organizations, and teams that rely on our technology to stay ahead of the race.

We are a Danish company founded, owned, and managed since 2003 by three entrepreneurs with a strong passion for sports. Today, we have a global footprint with our headquarters located in Denmark (Hørsholm) and offices in New York, Phoenix, Seoul and Tokyo. We employ over 1000+ people worldwide, half of which work in Denmark, where most hardware and software products are developed, tested, and manufactured.

**Where innovation happens

**At Trackman, we know that great people make great products. We believe that teams thrive, and innovation sparks in an atmosphere where people are encouraged to think for themselves, where everybody’s voices are heard, and where the best ideas prevail in the pursuit of exceptional solutions. This mix makes Trackman an inspiring company – for our customers and colleagues.

**Share our Passion!

**For additional information about the position, please contact our Electronics Team Lead, Søren Seehusen, at sts@trackman.com . Applications are continuously assessed, so please send your application as soon as possible.

jobs.occupation: BIOLOGIST - DHI MUSE AND AVIAN ECOLOGY
jobs.description:
Do you want to lead the ecological interpretation of complex offshore bird-monitoring projects? Can you turn radar, video, acoustic and environmental data into scientifically defensible conclusions for clients and regulators? Join DHI and take scientific ownership of projects at the intersection of avian ecology, technology and offshore wind.

Responsibilities and challenges

We are looking for a Biologist to support the scientific delivery of DHI MUSE and avian ecology projects. You will contribute to biological reviews, ecological analyses, reporting, and project coordination, working with experienced biologists, data scientists, instrumentation specialists and project managers. You will take increasing ownership of routine project-level scientific tasks, with guidance from senior colleagues and the Scientific Lead.

Your main responsibilities and challenges will include:

• Prepare, organise and analyse radar, video, acoustic, weather and system-status data needed for scientific deliverables.

• Contribute to ecological analyses of flight trajectories, bird flux, species distribution, phenology, avoidance behaviour and collision risk.

• Work with data scientists and analysts to review results and interpret them in their ecological context.

• Draft report sections, technical notes, presentations, figures, tables and responses to review comments.

• Document assumptions, uncertainty, limitations and other performance aspects clearly and consistently.

• Participate in project meetings and support communication with clients, suppliers, subcontractors and other DHI teams.

• Follow approved methods and quality procedures, and escalate unsupported conclusions or non-standard methods to senior colleagues.

Qualifications and personal skills

We are looking for a colleague with the following qualifications:

Required:

• Master's degree in biology, ecology, ornithology or a closely related discipline, equivalent relevant qualifications or other proven merits and references in ornithology.

• A strong foundation in avian ecology, species identification, animal behaviour, migration ecology or environmental monitoring.

• Ability to analyse scientific information and communicate findings clearly in writing and orally.

• Good data-handling skills and willingness to work with radar, video, acoustic and environmental datasets.

• Ability to collaborate across biological, analytical, technical and project-management disciplines.

• Ability to use AI to speed up delivery without loss of quality.

Desirable:

• Relevant professional, internship, thesis or research experience in bird monitoring, ecological consultancy or offshore wind.

• Experience reviewing wildlife video or acoustic recordings, identifying birds, or working with behavioural annotations.

• Experience in R, Python or other tools used for data analysis.

• Knowledge of environmental impact assessment, collision-risk modelling or remote-sensing methods.

Personal qualities:

• Curious, methodical and keen to learn.

• Self-motivated and comfortable asking for guidance when needed.

• Strong attention to detail and scientific integrity.

• Collaborative, service-minded and able to communicate with colleagues from different disciplines.

We offer

To work at DHI means being part of an organisation that addresses complex challenges in water and the environment. We will offer you:

• A role where ecological science is applied directly to offshore wind and environmental decision-making.

• Collaboration with biologists, data scientists, analysts, instrumentation specialists and project managers.

• Professional and personal development, with room to grow your scientific and client-facing responsibilities.

• Flexible working opportunities.

About DHI and DHI MUSE

DHI is a global and independent company dedicated to working on challenges within the fields of water and environment and sustainability. Within these fields, we provide a wide range of advisory, digital advisory, research and water governance services as well as providing leading edge MIKE and MUSE technologies and products to the market. jobs.occupation: Interdisciplinary Postdoctoral Fellow in Host-Directed Antimicrobial Research
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a one-year position to commence 1 March 2027 or after agreement.

  Introduction

  Antimicrobial resistance is a growing global health challenge that highlights the need for innovative therapeutic strategies beyond conventional antibiotic treatment.

  Host-directed antimicrobial strategies are attracting increasing interest as complementary approaches to conventional antimicrobial therapy. Recent studies have demonstrated that a novel synthetic compound improves survival in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA)-infected Caenorhabditis elegans. Furthermore, previous studies in mammalian cells suggest that the compound may exert immunomodulatory effects, raising the possibility that stimulation of host defence pathways contributes to protection against infection.

  This project aims to determine whether the novel synthetic compound can stimulate innate immunity and enhance host defence pathways in C. elegans and thereby contribute to protection against MRSA-infection. Using a combination of immunology, microbiology, and transcriptomics, the successful candidate will lead the experimental investigation of the phenotypic and transcriptional responses underlying this protective effect. All experimental work will be conducted in C. elegans.

  Required qualifications

   	
• A PhD in immunology, infection biology, microbiology, molecular biology, biomedical sciences, pharmacology, or a related discipline. 	
• Hands-on experience with the maintenance and experimental use of Caenorhabditis elegans, preferably as an infection model. 	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways. 	
• Demonstrated ability to conduct independent research. 	
• Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.   Highly desirable qualifications

   	
• Knowledge to innate immunity and host defence pathways in Caenorhabditis elegans. 	
• Experience with bacterial culture and experimental microbiology. 	
• Experience with omics-data analysis (such as RNA-seq data). 	
• Experience with quantitative PCR (qPCR) and gene expression analysis. 	
• Experience with RNA interference (RNAi) and gene-silencing approaches. 	
• Knowledge of antimicrobial compounds and antimicrobial resistance. 	
• Experience contributing to external funding applications. 	
• A strong publication record relative to career stage.   Key responsibilities

  The postdoctoral fellow will conduct research within host-directed antimicrobial strategies and innate immunity. The successful candidate is expected to contribute to student supervision, assist in the preparation of external funding applications, and lead the dissemination of research findings through scientific publications and presentations, as well as participate in other academic activities.

  Research environment and collaboration 

  The successful candidate will be based in a research environment with expertise in C. elegans biology and will interact closely with collaborators possessing complementary expertise in immunity, microbiology, and bioinformatics. jobs.description:
The Department of Anthropology, School of Culture and Society, invites applications for a three-year position as assistant professor in relation to the research project “Stories from my new life: Mobile transitions and social becomings among resettled refugees in Denmark” (TRANSIT).

An assistant professorship is a full-time, three-year training position that involves research and teaching at the BA and MA level and includes an obligatory course in university teaching for assistant professors. The position will commence on 1 February, 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

Place of employment: Department of Anthropology, Moesgaard Allé 20, 8270 Højbjerg, Denmark.

The Faculty of Arts is committed to creating an inclusive working environment and therefore encourages all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of personal background, gender, sexual orientation, age, disability, ethnicity etc.

The position
The position will be associated with the research project TRANSIT at the Department of Anthropology and is a combined teaching and research position.

Here is a brief description of the TRANSIT project:

In 2021-2024 app. 600 Congolese women and children were resettled in Denmark under the UNHCR resettlement program. TRANSIT is concerned with resettled refugees’ life transitions, understood as a set of complex legal, social and existential transitions that are particularly urgent in the context of resettlement: 1) the transition from youth to adulthood; 2) the transition from being single to being married; and 3) the transition into old age and, ultimately, death. The project aims to establish a collaboration between Aarhus University, VIVE – The Danish Center for Social Science Research, FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark, DFUNK – Dansk Flygtningehjælp Ungdom and a large group of resettled families in order to: a) create a mobile pop-up exhibition to be presented across Denmark in 2029; b) develop research-based teaching materials for pupils in the final years of Folkeskolen and in Gymnasiet on what it means to be resettled and start a new life in Denmark; and c) publish articles in leading peer-reviewed journals – based on a range of qualitative and quantitative data – on storytelling and life transitions following resettlement.

The selected candidate is expected to do individual fieldwork, be main responsible for a work-package (developing research-based teaching material with FLUGT – Refugee Museum of Denmark), and to be a dedicated member of the project team and engaged in all the project activities and responsibilities.

The position is offered with a view to attracting qualified applicants with an established and well-documented research record in innovative and internationally recognized research within anthropology and a specialization in migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination. 

Research
The selected applicant will be expected to contribute to core activities at the School of Culture and Society and Aarhus University in general and contribute to the Department of Anthropology’s research activities and output in particular. They will be expected to take an interest in interdisciplinary research collaboration within the Department of Anthropology, the School of Culture and Society, the Faculty of Arts, and beyond. 

The selected applicant will also be expected to develop new research projects with internal and external partners and to raise external research funding. The applicant’s research credentials and publication record within the field, e.g. anthropology, migration and refugee studies, collaborative methods and creative forms of research dissemination, will be assessed not just on existing publications and other research contributions but also on research potential.

Past research output will be assessed based on the active research time of the applicant in question. We therefore ask applicants to specify any career breaks they have had (for instance due to maternity/paternity leave or sick leave) so we may discount these periods when assessing research productivity.

Teaching
The position will involve some teaching (up to 33% of the time) as agreed upon with the Head of the Department and the project PI. The selected applicant will be required to teach and supervise at BA and MA levels of the department’s degree programs in Anthropology and Human Security and will be expected to have teaching experience at university level. 

We emphasise the importance of maintaining a professional and respectful relationship between staff and students, so applicants should be able to demonstrate and exemplify their commitment to participatory teaching initiatives and student involvement as part of their teaching portfolio.

Qualifications
Applicants must hold a PhD or equivalent qualifications in anthropology or a related discipline. They must also be able to document the following: 

• An internationally oriented research profile documented through relevant academic publications, and possibly other research contributions, at the international level
• Experience of university-level teaching and a commitment to teaching development and the supervision of student projects
• Experience of or interest in active participation in international research collaboration
• Experience of or interest in obtaining external research funding
• Experience of or interest in research dessimination for a non-academic audience
Applicants are asked to submit:

• A concise statement of motivation for applying for the position, including a description of experience with public research dessimination (maximum two pages).
• A full CV (one page).
• A full publication list (research outputs and public dissemination)
• A maximum of two publications.
Only submitted publications will be assessed; a list of publications is not sufficient. As a result, applications without submitted publications will not be assessed.

References or recommendations should not be included with the application. Applicants who are selected for a job interview may be asked to provide professional references.

Language and further information
Applicants can teach and supervise in English at university level.

If the selected applicant is not fluent in Danish, they will be expected to acquire the language within a period of approximately two years. 

To maintain and develop the department’s research environment, the person appointed is expected to be present at the department on a regular basis.

Applications must be uploaded in English.

For further information about the TRANSIT project (including the project description), please contact, PI, Professor Mikkel Rytter, mikkel.rytter@cas.au.dk

For further information about the application procedure, please contact Human Resources: iks-hr-sag@au.dk.

Knowledge exchange
It is expected that the selected applicant will engage in knowledge exchange as described in the strategy for the Faculty of Arts Strategy Arts 2020-2025 (au.dk), for instance research cooperation with private companies, government consultancy, cooperation with civil society partners or the public dissemination of knowledge. Applicants should document any prior experience within the field of knowledge exchange.

School of Culture and Society
The School of Culture and Society is a vibrant research community engaged in understanding the cultural and social conditions that shape human life. Our work examines how people interact with their environments, from prehistory to the present and across both local and global contexts. Through cross-sector and cross-disciplinary partnerships, we aim to support research innovation and contribute to addressing the major questions facing society. In both research and education, we are committed to bringing the humanities into active dialogue with partners beyond the university.

The School is committed to:

Read more about the school here School of Culture and Society - Aarhus University

International applicants

About Arts
The Faculty of Arts is one of Northern Europe’s most significant faculties for research and higher education in the humanities, theology and education. jobs.description:
Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences

  University of Copenhagen

   

  The University seeks to appoint an time limited associate professor at the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology to commence March 1st 2025 or as soon as possible thereafter

  Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology is committed to advancing human health through discovery, design, and evaluation of safe and effective medical treatments. To achieve this, we work in a dynamic and committed academic community, that bridges health science and life science in a translational and innovative approach from molecule to patient. We value interdisciplinary research and education, development of individual competences, and finding solutions to todays and tomorrows challenges in society. The department furthermore prioritizes sustainability in all aspects of research and education.

  The department is organized in six research sections and furthermore houses Center for Pharmaceutical Data Science Education and Center for Protein Design. Further information on the Department can be found at: https://drug.ku.dk/

  Job description 

  We seek an established researcher to lead an independent research programme at the interface of clinical proteomics, molecular neuropathology, and translational neuroscience. The successful candidate will drive biofluid biomarker discovery and drug-target identification in Huntington’s disease and other neurodegenerative disorders, contributing to the department’s data-driven target and drug discovery activities and to its concerted effort to integrate data science and AI into research and teaching. Using state-of-the-art mass spectrometry-based proteomics, multi-omics, and machine learning, the candidate will connect mechanistic insight to clinical application through disease-relevant models and human sample cohorts, supporting AI-powered translational prediction and clinical decision support for personalized treatment.

  Responsibilities

  The associate professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination of results to the scientific community and attraction of external funding 	
• Develop, organize, and conduct research-based teaching, including associated examination. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of students and researchers 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments 	
• Engage in outreach and/or innovation activities both within the Department and towards academia, the clinic, and industry in general.   Qualifications of the applicant

  When evaluating applicants, primary emphasis will be placed on the applicant's ability to document original scientific work of the highest international standard, an innovative mindset, and strong ambitions for advancing teaching within the fields of biochemistry and pharmacology, with particular focus on teaching on compulsory courses at the BSc and MSc levels.

  Applicants already having sustainability integrated in all aspects of their research and teaching, or a clear plan for doing so, will have preference. Likewise, a clear and structured plan for internal and external collaborations will be given positive consideration.

  Overall criteria for the position: 

  To be qualified for an associate professor position, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, teaching, innovation & societal impact, organisational contribution and leadership. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to document:

   	
• Research qualifications at the level that can be achieved by satisfactorily completing a period of employment as an assistant professor/postdoc, but may also be obtained in other ways 	
• Teaching qualifications and pedagogical competencies 	
• Research-based teaching   The associate professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Desired qualifications: 

   	
• Strong, independent research record in neurodegenerative disease, with expertise in mass spectrometry-based proteomics and biofluid biomarker discovery. 	
• Experience integrating multi-omics data with machine learning and AI, and working with preclinical models and cell-type-resolved approaches. 	
• A track record of securing competitive external funding and of research leadership. 	
• Teaching experience and formal teaching qualifications (e.g. Universitetspædagogikum), together with supervision experience. 	
• Ability to bridge discovery and translation (from molecule to patient) and to collaborate across academia, clinic, and industry, including innovation and spin-out activity   Terms of employment
 The position is a time limited position for 5 years. The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish). 

  The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.
 
 Questions
 For further information, please contact Head of Department Dan Stærk, ds@sund.ku.dk. For information about the Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology and the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences (SUND), please see www.drug.ku.dk and https://sund.ku.dk/.

  
 Foreign applicants may find this link useful: https://www.ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility).
 
 Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application, including motivations for applying for the position (maximum 1 page) 	
• Curriculum vitae, including information about external funding 	
• Diplomas (Master’s, PhD, and other relevant certificates) 	
• A complete list of publications 	
• Research plan (3-5 pages) 	
• Uploads of maximum 5 (associate professors) publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Teaching plan 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines: https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/job-application-portfolio)   Application procedure
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee.  All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee, and each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at The university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship in antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) engineering: internalization and lysosomal delivery
jobs.description:
Biotech Research and Innovation Centre (BRIC) / Finsen Laboratory, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen

  A 3-year PhD fellowship is available in the research group of Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm. Expected start: 15 January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

   

  The project

  Antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs) depend on efficient internalization and lysosomal processing to release their cytotoxic payload. Inefficient trafficking limits potency and restricts current ADCs to targets with very high receptor density. The PhD project will engineer and test next-generation ADCs with improved internalization and lysosomal routing. This includes bispecific constructs that combine our established ADC targets (uPAR, MMP14, uPARAP and the Mannose Receptor) with receptors that drive lysosomal delivery, such as IGF2R. Lead candidates will be evaluated in cancer cell models and in vivo, including models of sarcoma and glioblastoma.

  The project is part of the Novo Nordisk Foundation Distinguished Innovator project "Breaking Barriers: Engineering ADCs for Efficient BBB Transport and Lysosomal Targeting", in collaboration with Professor Matthias Herth (Department of Drug Design and Pharmacology, UCPH) and Professor Katrine Qvortrup (Department of Chemistry, DTU).

   

  Main tasks

   	
•  	Production, purification and validation of recombinant and bispecific antibodies

 	 	
•  	Conjugation of antibodies to cytotoxic payloads and characterization of the resulting ADCs

 	 	
•  	Cell-based assays: antibody uptake and internalization, flow cytometry, drug screening and cytotoxicity/cell viability assays

 	 	
•  	In vivo efficacy studies of ADC candidates in tumor models

 	 	
•  	Writing scientific publications and presenting at international conferences

 	    

   

  Job description
 Your key tasks as a PhD student at SUND are:

   	
•  	Carrying through an independent research project under supervision.

•  	Participating in active research environments including a stay at another research team.

 	 	
•  	Obtaining experience with teaching or other types of dissemination related to your PhD project

 	 	
•  	Teaching and disseminating your knowledge.

 	 	
•  	Writing a PhD thesis on the grounds of your project

 	    

  PhD Programme Description:
 The PhD programme is a three-year full-time research education within the framework of the 5+3 scheme, intended for candidates holding a relevant academic degree within the project’s subject area (e.g., [relevant degrees]).

   

  Qualifications

  We are looking for a candidate with a strong, hands-on background in ADC research. Applicants must have:

   	
•  	An MSc degree (120 ECTS, or equivalent) in pharmaceutical biotechnology, biotechnology or a closely related field, with an excellent academic record

 	 	
•  	An MSc thesis or equivalent research project on antibody-drug conjugates or antibody-based cancer therapeutics

 	 	
•  	Documented hands-on experience with production, validation and payload conjugation of recombinant antibodies

 	 	
•  	Experience with cytotoxicity, cell viability and drug screening assays in mammalian cancer cell lines

 	 	
•  	Experience with flow cytometry

 	 	
•  	Experience with laboratory animal work

 	 	
•  	Experience from an international research laboratory and excellent written and spoken English

 	   Experience with functional genomics (e.g. CRISPR-Cas9 screening) and with sarcoma models is an advantage.

     Place of employment

  The place of employment is BRIC, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. We offer creative and stimulating working conditions in dynamic and international research environment. 

   

  Terms of employment 
 The average weekly working hours are 37 hours per week.

  The position is a fixed-term position limited to a period of 3 years. The start date is 15 January 2027 or after agreement.

  The employment is conditioned upon the applicant’s successful enrolment as a PhD student at the Graduate School at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  The PhD study must be completed in accordance with The Ministerial Order on the PhD programme (2013) and the Faculty’s rules on achieving the degree. 

  Salary, pension and terms of employment are in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. Depending on seniority, the monthly salary starts at approximately 31,800 DKK/Roughly 4,200 EUR (August 2026 level) plus pension.

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

   

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Associate Professor Lars Henning Engelholm, lhe@finsenlab.dk.

  General information about PhD studies at the Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences is available at the Graduate School’s website: https://healthsciences.ku.dk/phd/guidelines/

   

  Application procedure
 Your application must be submitted electronically by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. The application must include the following documents in PDF format: 

  1. Motivated letter of application (max. one page)

  2. CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position

  3. Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in other language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufm.dk/en/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database. Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science

  4. Publication list (if possible)

jobs.description:
Planetary is looking for a Managing Director (Fondsdirektør) to lead Planetary A/S and the continued development of its two investment funds: Planetary Impact Ventures and Planetary Soil Fund.

At Planetary, we invest in companies and farmland aligned with our guiding principles. We invest in companies with a focus on long-term business models within planetary boundaries, and in degraded farmland and partners who are committed to soil regeneration. Our commitment is manifested in our evergreen structure. Our focus is biodiversity, agriculture and food, and we aim to provide a fair financial return. We want to inspire and contribute to a restructuring of our economic systems, a redefinition of what value is, and increase our understanding and reconnection with nature and life on the planet.

At Planetary, our work does not stop with investments. Our theory of change is focusing on a systemic and broad approach. We work to nourish and contribute to the community around us. We believe that value alignment between investors, us as intermediaries, and our portfolio companies is essential to the success of our shared mission. These principles are instrumental to the way we work – and who we are.

The role

As Managing Director, you will have the overall responsibility for Planetary A/S, ensuring strong governance and compliance, performance and development of the funds. You will report to the Board, and work closely with all the people working at Planetary.

Your work will be grounded in a deep commitment to systems change and a transition towards organic-regenerative food and agriculture.

·      Support founders and management teams of the companies where Planetary can contribute experience, perspective and network.

·      Maintain oversight of portfolio performance, risks, opportunities and capital requirements.

·      Take board roles in portfolio companies.

You have:

·      Experience with investing.

·      Proven track record in operational leadership and business development.

·      Strong analytical and financial management skills.

·      Experience in people leadership and organisational development.

·      Good communication, interpersonal skills and stakeholder management abilities.

·      A deeply rooted commitment to contributing to a healthier planet.

You are likely to have:

·      Several years’ experience from venture capital, impact investment, private equity or another relevant investment environment.

·      A solid understanding of fund economics, fund raising, portfolio performance and investments.

·      An understanding of impact management and the integration of financial and impact objectives.

Experience within food and organic-regenerative agriculture is an advantage, but not a prerequisite. Commitment to transforming the food system towards a more regenerative and resilient future is essential.

The right candidate

You are an experienced leader with a strong understanding of investments and of how capital can contribute to systemic change.

You combine sound judgement and the ability to create momentum with curiosity, collaboration and humility. You enjoy working in a small organisation where people remain close to the work and are motivated by long-term development.

__________________________________________________________________________

Location

Our office is at an organic farm in Humlebæk.

Timeline and application

Please apply before November 6th, 2026. Applications should be sent to Annette Hartvig Bohé at ahb@planetary.dk . Applications will be evaluated on an ongoing basis.

Questions

If you have questions about the job, feel free to reach out to Chair Jacob Jelsing, jj@planetary.dk, or Director Annette Hartvig Bohé, ahb@planetary.dk

Our guiding principles

Stay humble: Seeking to understand and improve the conditions for life on the planet is a task of infinite complexity. Grounded by nature, we stay humble and sincere in everything we do.

Learn with nature: Inspiration in nature and its biological processes will guide our investments. We shall adapt ourselves to nature, rather than forcing nature to comply with us.

Perceive wealth holistically: True wealth is much more than money in the bank. We perceive wealth as well-being and harmony between humans, nature and the economy.

Trust patient capital: Real value takes time to manifest. We support long-term business models and real value creation over quick profit maximisation.

Build strong communities: Strong communities build resilience and awareness. We strive to create movement and stronger connections within the networks we grow with.

Advocate for change: Real change depends on systemic change. We dedicate ourselves to create real, tangible change and assume leadership towards a new paradigm.
